summary: The builder reported that `npm run build` still fails. On this machine the file it points at does not exist, and on the current working tree `npm run build` (rollup -c), `npm run type-check` and `npm test` all pass and produce dist/index.js and dist/index.mjs including the already-decided light/dark/system theme work. The one publish-gate check that is actually failing is `npm run validate-package` (attw --pack . && publint): attw reports the ESM entry as "Masquerading as CJS" (FalseCJS), which would stop `npm publish`. The requirement is therefore to make the library publishable from a clean state: the build must finish green from a clean state and the package must pass its publish checks, with no new product behaviour. Only the build/publish definitions of done are requested.
roles: Library maintainer: runs `npm run build` and `npm run validate-package` to produce and publish the package to npm
Library consumer (developer who installs the package): receives built JavaScript and type declarations that resolve correctly for both `import` and `require`

requirements.text: Running `npm run build` in the library root from a clean state (the dist folder deleted) finishes with exit code 0 and produces dist/index.js, dist/index.mjs and the TypeScript declaration files, with no errors.
requirements.rationale: The builder reported a failing build, and a library that cannot be built cannot be published. Every other change, including the already-approved light/dark/system theme work, is blocked until the build is reliably green.
acceptance: From a clean checkout (dist removed, dependencies installed), `npm run build` exits with code 0
dist/index.js and dist/index.mjs exist after the build
`npm test` still passes after any change made to fix the build
edgeCases: The build must pass from a clean state (dist deleted), not only when an old dist folder is already present

If a build error can only be reproduced under conditions other than the current tree, for example a different Node version, the error message and cause must be recorded rather than the build declared fixed without evidence
The theme feature's CSS and TypeScript changes must not introduce build or type errors
pitfalls: Fixing the build must not remove or change any exported component, prop or type
The build must not be made to pass by disabling checks, type-checking or tests

requirements.text: Running `npm run validate-package` (attw --pack . && publint) finishes with exit code 0 for the packaged library, with TypeScript able to resolve correct declaration kinds for both `import` and `require` consumers and no entry reported as masquerading as another module kind.
requirements.rationale: This is the check that actually fails today and the step that runs before publishing (`prepublishOnly`), so a developer still cannot publish even though `npm run build` passes. attw currently reports node16 (from ESM): "Masquerading as CJS" (FalseCJS) for the main entry, meaning an ESM import resolves the type declaration as CommonJS while the JavaScript is ESM.
acceptance: For the `jattac.libs.web.responsive-table` entry, attw reports node16 (from ESM) and node16 (from CJS) both green (no "Masquerading as CJS")
The check stays green when run against an output built fresh from a clean state (dist deleted first)
edgeCases: The check must pass on a freshly built package, not only against a previously built dist folder
A fix for the ESM resolution must not regress the CommonJS entry (node16 from CJS must stay green)
The check must pass in CI as well as locally, where the working tree may start with no dist folder
pitfalls: Do not silence attw with ignore flags or by dropping the ESM build; that would hide a real consumer-facing problem rather than fix it
Do not change or remove any public export, prop or type to make the check pass
Do not pin or downgrade dependencies merely to dodge the check

outOfScope: Any new feature or visual change
Creating missing scaffolding such as .size-limit.json, scripts/check-docs.mjs or scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs
Upgrading dependencies beyond what is needed to make the build and package checks pass
Changing the library's public API, exports or rendered output

nonFunctional.statement: The build and package check give the same result on repeated runs from a clean state.
nonFunctional.acceptance: Running `npm run build` then `npm run validate-package` twice in a row, deleting dist before the first run, exits with code 0 both times.

risks: The reported npm debug log does not exist on this machine, so the original failure message cannot be read; the only reproducible failing publish check is `npm run validate-package` (attw FalseCJS).
The previous run was marked complete while `npm run validate-package` still failed, so the packaging fix may not have been attempted; if the working tree changes are reverted, the failure returns.
A narrow fix to the ESM declaration resolution could regress the CommonJS entry if both are not verified.
glossary: Build: `rollup -c`, which bundles src/index.tsx into dist/index.js and dist/index.mjs.
validate-package: `attw --pack . && publint`, run by `prepublishOnly`; attw checks how the published package's JavaScript and type declarations resolve for common consumers.
Masquerading as CJS (FalseCJS): attw's report that an ESM import resolves to a CommonJS-style type declaration while the runtime JavaScript is ESM.

coverage.note: Library maintainer runs the build and publish checks; developers who install the package are the consumers. The request comes from the builder.
No data is stored; this is a build/packaging fix.
No records or access control involved.
No end-user input; the only validation is the package check itself, covered by R2.
The only states are each check succeeding or failing with a readable error.
Nothing is deleted by users; dist is removed only to prove a clean build.
No personal or sensitive data involved.
Reliability and packaging correctness only: build and package checks are repeatable from a clean state and types resolve for both module systems.

assumptions: The builder's "npm run build still failing" refers to the publish pipeline, whose reproducible failing step is `npm run validate-package`; `npm run build` itself exits 0 today.

Success means `npm run build`, `npm run type-check`, `npm test` and `npm run validate-package` all exit 0 from a clean state, not a size budget or docs check, since the project has no scripts for those.
The already-decided light/dark/system theme work stays as it is; this change only makes the build and package checks green without altering its behaviour.
